input.question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?
input.ground_truth: Some people can do just that. Otherwise, it just fucks with your brain trying to put two images from both eyes at different angles together. Crossing out eyes focuses on something in front of us. Making the eyes look in their own direction doesn't do us any good for survival, so the skill never really evolved

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are we able to cross our eyes and unable to do the opposite?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your eyes are like two little toy balls on springs. Your muscles help move your eyes.

When you want to cross your eyes, you use special muscles to make them move toward each other. That’s easy because those muscles can work together.

But if you try to make your eyes look far away from each other—like trying to push your eyes out of your head—it’s hard! That’s because your eyes are attached to your face, and your muscles aren’t made to pull them apart. They’re better at moving toward each other or looking up, down, or to the sides.

So, you can cross your eyes easily, but you can’t make them go far apart like that.
